flags: Both archived tourism pages give 220 miles in prose and 245 miles in their length field; material maps 229.5. Omitted total distance because the cache does not resolve scope.

No source describes the byway’s founding, campaign, road construction or designation date. Historical paragraph covers documented landscape and park-access development, without presenting those events as creation of the byway.

Sequence follows supplied strip anchors: Alexandria, Glenwood, Sunburg/Monson, Willmar, New London/Sibley, Terrace, Sauk Centre. The network has multiple loops; this is one reading order, not a claim that the byway has two fixed endpoints.

Monson’s conflict and commemoration history has only a secondary source in the cache, with no Dakota-authored account or underlying treaty records. Used measured summary and included documented Dakota hardship; omitted detailed attack narrative.
Sibley moment is shorter because the cached article offers limited building history. No access, fee or seasonal-driving claim is made from archived tourism or secondary park sources.
